questions.prompt: Which spirit is the main base of a classic margarita?
questions.clue: It is distilled from the agave plant.
questions.explanation: A classic margarita is tequila, orange liqueur, and lime juice.

questions.prompt: Who wrote the novel "1984"?
questions.clue: Same author as Animal Farm.
questions.explanation: George Orwell published Nineteen Eighty-Four in 1949.

questions.prompt: In poker, what is a "full house"?
options: Three of a kind plus a pair
questions.clue: Also called a "full boat" — three matching + two matching.
questions.explanation: A full house is three cards of one rank and two of another.

questions.prompt: What does "IPA" stand for in craft beer?
questions.clue: Historically linked to British beer shipped toward South Asia.
questions.explanation: IPA stands for India Pale Ale.

questions.prompt: Which film won the Academy Award for Best Picture in 1994 (ceremony for 1993 films)?
questions.clue: Steven Spielberg's Holocaust drama.
questions.explanation: Schindler's List won Best Picture at the 66th Academy Awards.

questions.prompt: What is the legal drinking age in the United States (federal standard for purchase)?
questions.clue: Raised nationwide in the 1980s via highway funding rules.
questions.explanation: The National Minimum Drinking Age Act established 21 for purchase.

questions.prompt: Which city is traditionally associated with Mardi Gras celebrations in the U.S.?
questions.clue: Think jazz, French Quarter, and beads.
questions.explanation: New Orleans is famous for its Mardi Gras carnival.

questions.prompt: Compared to the same volume of drip coffee, espresso is typically:
options: Identical in caffeine per ounce always
questions.clue: It is a concentrated extraction; a full mug of drip often has more total caffeine.
questions.explanation: Espresso is more concentrated per ounce, though serving sizes differ so totals vary.

questions.prompt: Which economist wrote "The Wealth of Nations" (1776)?
questions.clue: Often called the father of modern economics; Scottish Enlightenment.
questions.explanation: Adam Smith published An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations in 1776.

questions.prompt: What does "BYOB" usually mean on a party invite?
questions.clue: Hosts are not providing drinks.
questions.explanation: BYOB commonly means bring your own bottle (alcohol).

questions.prompt: A standard bottle of wine is about how many milliliters?
questions.clue: It is three-quarters of a liter.
questions.explanation: Most still wine bottles are 750 ml.

questions.prompt: How many cards are in a standard deck (no jokers)?
questions.clue: Four suits of 13 ranks each.
questions.explanation: A standard deck has 52 cards.

questions.prompt: Roughly what percentage of Earth's surface is covered by water?
questions.clue: Often summarized as "about seven-tenths".
questions.explanation: Oceans and other water cover about 71% of Earth's surface.

questions.prompt: About how many minutes of gameplay are in a regulation NBA quarter?
questions.clue: Four of these make a regulation game before overtime.
questions.explanation: NBA quarters are 12 minutes each.

questions.prompt: A "fifth" of liquor is historically about how many ounces?
questions.clue: Named for one-fifth of a U.S. gallon.
questions.explanation: A fifth is 1/5 gallon ≈ 25.6 U.S. fl oz (today often sold as 750 ml).

questions.prompt: How many squares are on a standard chessboard?
questions.clue: It is an 8×8 grid.
questions.explanation: A chessboard has 64 squares.

questions.prompt: Approximate ABV of most mainstream lagers (beer)?
questions.clue: Much lower than spirits; higher than most kombucha.
questions.explanation: Many lagers sit around 4–6% alcohol by volume.

questions.prompt: How many holes are on a standard golf course round?
questions.clue: A "full round" is double a short-course loop.
questions.explanation: A standard course round is 18 holes.

questions.prompt: In casino roulette (European), a single-number bet pays 35:1. If you bet $1 and win, your profit is:
questions.clue: 35:1 means 35 units of profit, stake returned separately.
questions.explanation: At 35:1 you win $35 profit (plus your $1 stake back as $36 total returned).

questions.prompt: If every member of a club is over 21, and Sam is a member, then:
questions.clue: Universal rule applied to a specific member.
questions.explanation: If all members are over 21 and Sam is a member, Sam is over 21.

questions.prompt: A fair coin is flipped twice. Probability of two heads?
questions.clue: Independent flips: multiply probabilities.

questions.prompt: "Only managers have keys. Jordan has a key." What follows?
options: Jordan might be an intern with a spare
questions.clue: "Only managers have keys" means anyone with a key must be a manager.
questions.explanation: If only managers have keys and Jordan has a key, Jordan is a manager.

questions.prompt: Which number is the odd one out: 3, 5, 7, 9, 11?
questions.clue: Four are prime; one is composite.
questions.explanation: 9 = 3×3 is not prime; the others are prime.

questions.prompt: If interest compounds annually at 100% on $100 for 1 year, you end with:
questions.clue: Doubling once.
questions.explanation: 100% annual compound interest doubles the principal in one year → $200.

questions.prompt: There are 5 people at a party. Everyone shakes hands with everyone else once. How many handshakes?
questions.clue: Combinations: n(n-1)/2.
questions.explanation: C(5,2)=10 handshakes.

questions.prompt: A bartender says: "Happy hour is 4–7pm." It is 7:05pm. Is it happy hour?
options: Only if the clock is wrong
questions.clue: Exclusive end times are common: until 7 means ends at 7.
questions.explanation: At 7:05 the stated window has ended.

questions.prompt: Which came first historically?
options: Prohibition in the U.S. ends (21st Amendment)
World War II begins in Europe
questions.clue: Think early 1930s for the end of Prohibition.
questions.explanation: 21st Amendment ratified 1933; WWII 1939; Moon 1969; USSR 1991.

questions.prompt: Typical order in a three-course Western meal — which is first?
questions.clue: It whets the appetite.
questions.explanation: Appetizer/starter comes before the main and dessert.

questions.prompt: Which Beatles album was released first?
options: Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band
questions.clue: Their debut studio album (1963).
questions.explanation: Please Please Me (1963) preceded the later classic albums listed.

questions.prompt: Which step comes first when brewing pour-over coffee?
options: Pour all water at once blindly
questions.clue: You need grounds before extraction.
questions.explanation: Beans are ground (after weighing) before brewing.

questions.prompt: In a standard wine service sequence, which happens first?
options: Server empties the bottle into trash
questions.clue: You open before anyone tastes.
questions.explanation: Opening (and often presenting the cork) precedes tasting.

questions.prompt: Which tax-year event usually comes earliest in the calendar year for U.S. filers?
options: Receiving W-2 forms (typically by end of January)
December 31 tax year end already passed
questions.clue: Employers must furnish W-2s early in the new year.
questions.explanation: Form W-2 is generally due to employees by January 31.

questions.prompt: What does "sommelier" primarily refer to?
questions.clue: Often certified to pair bottles with food.
questions.explanation: A sommelier is a trained wine professional, often in restaurants.

questions.prompt: Which cocktail traditionally includes mint, lime, sugar, soda, and rum?
questions.clue: Cuban origin; muddled mint is iconic.
questions.explanation: A mojito combines white rum, sugar, lime, soda water, and mint.

questions.prompt: A "proof" number for U.S. spirits is roughly how related to ABV?
questions.clue: 80 proof ≈ 40% ABV.
questions.explanation: In the U.S., proof is typically twice the alcohol by volume percentage.

questions.prompt: How many players start on the field per side in American football?
questions.clue: Same count as soccer, different sport.
questions.explanation: Eleven players per team are on the field at a time.

questions.prompt: Which streaming service launched earliest?
questions.clue: It started as a DVD rental mail service in the late 1990s.
questions.explanation: Netflix was founded in 1997; the other services launched decades later.

questions.prompt: If a bar tab is $40 and you tip 20%, tip amount is:
questions.clue: 20% of 40 is one-fifth.

questions.prompt: Which grape is traditionally the primary red grape of Burgundy, France?
questions.clue: Thin-skinned, elegant reds from cool climates.
questions.explanation: Burgundy reds are predominantly Pinot Noir.
